newsitem.title: USA: LecTec to restructure, sees Q3 charge.
newsitem.headline: LecTec to restructure, sees Q3 charge.

text.p: LecTec Corp said Monday its director had adopted a restructuring plan designed to result in the elimination of the company's Pharmadyne Corp subsidiary.
As a result of the restructuring, LecTec said it will record a non-recurring charge of about $1.5 million, or $0.39 a share, in the fiscal third quarter ending today.
LecTec develops, makes and markets products based on skin-interface technologies including diagnostic electrodes and over-the-counter analgesic patches.

The restructuring charge includes about $700,000 for the acquisition of the minority interests in Pharmadyne in exchange for newly issued shares of LecTec, and about $500,000 representing a write-off of the company's 15 percent interest in Natus LLC, a direct marketing company.
No further charges related to this restructuring are expected in future periods, LecTec said in a statement.

Rodney Young, LecTec chief executive officer and president, said the decision to eliminate Pharmadyne was the result of a business review that began last autumn following Young's August 1997 appointment to his current posts.
"The actions we are announcing today will bring us closer to our customers through a more efficient distribution system and should reduce our administrative costs," Young said in a statement.

"The restructuring is an important step toward achieving our corporate business goals of increasing sales to existing customers, expanding sales into new market segments while we effectively manage overall operations."
